content.title: Routing Changes the Screen Without Changing the Application
content.hook: A real application often has more than one screen:
content.context:
- `/` could be a home page.
- `/products` could be a product list.
- `/products/42` could be a product detail screen.

The important idea is simple:

**A route connects a location to the UI for that location.**

The user is still inside the same application. The current location changes, and the application chooses a different part of the UI to show.
goals: Understand a route as a mapping between a URL location and the UI that should be rendered for that location.

content.question:
A user is on `/products` and navigates to `/products/42`.

What should change?

options.text: The whole application has to forget all React components.
The current route changes, so the UI can switch to the product detail screen.
The browser must stop running JavaScript.
Every piece of state in the application must automatically disappear.

feedback.correct: A route change selects different UI. It does not mean the whole application is destroyed and rebuilt from nothing.
feedback.incorrect: A route change selects different UI. It does not mean the whole application is destroyed and rebuilt from nothing.

content.question:
Imagine this application has these routes:

```text
/                 → Home
/products         → ProductList
/products/42      → ProductDetail
/account          → Account
```

Which route should render for `/products/42`?

feedback.correct: The path points to the product detail route.
feedback.incorrect: The path points to the product detail route.

content.title: One application, many locations
content.text:
A useful mental model is:

```text
Current URL
    ↓
route matching
    ↓
selected UI
```

The route is not the UI itself. It is the rule that helps the application decide what UI belongs at the current location.

content.question:
A teammate says, “Routing is just changing buttons.”

What is missing?

options.text: Routing connects application locations to the UI that should be rendered there.

feedback.correct: Navigation may start with a click, but routing is about the relationship between location and application UI.
feedback.incorrect: Navigation may start with a click, but routing is about the relationship between location and application UI.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A route is a location-to-UI rule.
**Senior habit:** When a screen feels confusing, ask: “What location am I at, and which part of the application owns that location?”
